ConocoPhillips jumped 2.67% today, bouncing back from a three-day dip that had pushed the stock down 2.4% from its October 23 close. The move follows crude oil prices climbing sharply—US oil sitting at $103.37 per barrel today versus lower levels earlier in the week—likely driven by receding hopes for a near-term U.S.-Iran peace deal. Diplomatic talks in Tehran aimed at restarting negotiations had raised expectations for de-escalation, but recent political signals suggest a tougher stance may prevail after the midterm elections, reducing the likelihood of a quick deal that would ease oil supply concerns.

The broader context matters here: oil majors like this one benefit when crude prices rise, since higher prices expand the value of the barrels they produce. Over two weeks, the stock is up 5.13%, which tracks closely with the energy market's shift away from peace-deal optimism toward anticipation of continued geopolitical tension in the Middle East—a dynamic that keeps crude elevated and supports refiner and producer margins.
